reasons: Hand-written shapes can drift from the engine without a build failure, as the header comment admits.
Only the process record shape is generated from a schema.
No test that checks these shapes against the data is shown in the packet.

terms.meaning: A written description of what shape a piece of data must have, so a mistake is caught early.
A file produced by a tool from a schema, rather than typed by a person.
Full-time equivalent: one person working full time for one year.
A fixed sample of known cases that the tests use as reference data.
A number that ranks how trustworthy an evidence source is.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Explains the bundle types
sections.what: The header comment says this file gives types to the collected run data. It also explains that the process record comes from generated code, but the value and manifest shapes are written by hand and can drift.
sections.why: The comment states the gap openly: only the process record schema is exported for generation.
sections.watch_out: A change to the value or manifest output will not stop the build here. It will show up only when the viewer runs.

sections.name: Band
sections.title: Three-point range
sections.what: Defines a range as a low, base and high number.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely reason: most value figures are shown as ranges, so one shared shape keeps them consistent.

sections.name: Bridge
sections.title: Currency summary bridge
sections.what: Describes one currency's path from gross benefit through the three cost lines to net benefit, with the process ids and whether run costs are priced.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the field names. Likely reason: it lets a reader follow the arithmetic from gross to net.
sections.watch_out: When the run cost is not priced, the run cost figure is understated and the net is overstated.

sections.name: ProcessValue
sections.title: One process's value figures
sections.what: Describes one process: its wave, confidence, widening factor, evidence flag, effort ranges, realised fraction, horizon factor and gross benefit.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely reason: the process page reads these fields directly.
sections.watch_out: The horizon factor is a diagnostic. Engine tests say it must not be multiplied in again.

sections.name: WaveValue
sections.title: One delivery wave's totals
sections.what: Describes one wave: its number, start month, process ids, realised effort, gross benefit by currency and evidenced share.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely reason: the phasing view groups results by wave.

sections.name: EnablerPool
sections.title: Shared capability pool
sections.what: Describes a capability claimed by several processes: who claims it, the claims, the pool size, the weights and the credited effort.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely reason: the deduplication view shows how shared effort is split.
sections.watch_out: Weights must add to one. The engine tests check this, but this shape does not enforce it.

sections.name: PrerequisiteCost
sections.title: Cost of a needed prerequisite
sections.what: Describes a prerequisite: its reference, kind, the processes that need it, its wave, build effort, cost by currency and evidence ids.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely reason: prerequisite costs are shown on the bridge.

sections.name: RunCostBreakdown
sections.title: Running cost by category
sections.what: Describes yearly running cost per currency, split into inference, orchestration, monitoring and evaluation, model upkeep, and maintenance staff, plus whether the figures are priced.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely reason: it lets a reader see which running cost is largest.
sections.watch_out: When not priced, the figures show zero, which looks like a cheap system.

sections.name: Assumption
sections.title: A stated assumption with its basis
sections.what: Describes one assumption with its name, value, basis text and evidence ids.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely reason: the viewer shows what each number rests on.

sections.name: SensitivityResult
sections.title: One driver's effect on net benefit
sections.what: Records the net benefit at the low and high settings of one driver, and the swing between them.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely reason: the sensitivity view ranks drivers by swing.

sections.name: BaselineTie
sections.title: Client baseline comparison row
sections.what: Compares a client's net benefit with its revenue and earnings, giving the shares and a flag for implausible results.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely reason: it lets a reader judge whether the benefit is plausible for the client.
sections.watch_out: The implausible flag is the only warning in this shape, so check it when reading.

sections.name: PortfolioValue
sections.title: Whole portfolio value summary
sections.what: Describes the top-level value output: depth tier, duplication ratio, evidenced share, gross and deduplicated effort, realised effort, processes, pools, waves, prerequisite costs, run costs, bridges, sensitivities, reconciliation and assumptions.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely reason: this is the single shape the value view reads from.
sections.watch_out: This shape is hand-written, so a schema change will not be caught at build time.

sections.name: RunManifest
sections.title: Run record details
sections.what: Describes the run manifest: run id, schema version, dates, engagement, depth tier, taxonomy and ontology versions, knowledge snapshot, model ids, prompt versions and prefix hash.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely reason: the run stamp and provenance view read these fields.

sections.name: EvidenceItem
sections.title: One evidence item
sections.what: Describes one piece of evidence: its id, store, source reference, publication date, authority tier and excerpt.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely reason: evidence cards and chips display these fields.
sections.watch_out: If a field is removed here, the data is still present but not shown, and no error appears.

sections.name: PrerequisiteEdge
sections.title: Link between prerequisite and successor
sections.what: Describes one prerequisite edge: the predecessor, the successor, the reason and the evidence ids.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely reason: the wave plan and its explanations use these edges.

sections.name: GoldenCase
sections.title: A sample case with its evidence
sections.what: Describes one golden case: industry, case id, process id, depth tier, reason it was chosen, an optional evidence gap note, client finance context and its evidence pack.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely reason: the golden cases are the fixed reference examples the tests and the process view use.
sections.watch_out: The evidence gap note is optional, so the views must handle its absence.

sections.name: Artifacts
sections.title: Whole bundle type
sections.what: Describes the top-level bundle: collected sources, records, the value output, the manifest, the portfolio reconciliation with its edges, enabler attributions, the capacity check and cycles, and the golden cases.
sections.why: The comment explains that attribution fields were once missing from this shape, so claimant weights showed with no citation. Dropping fields from hand-written types hides data silently.
sections.watch_out: A missing field here hides data without any error. Compare with the export whenever the bundle changes.

summary: Defines the shape of the bundled run data that the viewer reads, including value results, the run manifest, evidence items and golden cases.
purpose: Gives the viewer a typed description of its input so editors can check field names, and so views know what to expect.
why: The header comment says process records come from generated types, but the value and manifest shapes are written by hand. The comment calls this a known gap rather than an oversight.
how: The file imports the process record type from generated code. It then declares a series of named shapes, one for each piece of the value output and the manifest, and finally one combined Artifacts shape that every view receives.
inputs: Nothing is run. This file only describes shapes.
outputs: Type information used at build time by the other frontend files.
risks: Types written by hand are not checked against the Python export. A changed field in the engine can therefore show up as a mismatch at run time rather than a build failure. A field dropped from a type disappears from the view without any error.
debug: If a view shows empty values, compare its field names with the shapes here and with the exported data. If a view fails at run time, check that the artifacts file matches the Artifacts shape.
